newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lippo sells China assets for HK$697 mln.
newsitem.headline: Lippo sells China assets for HK$697 mln.

text.p: Lippo Ltd said on Monday it had agreed to sell property development projects in China to China Travel Service (Holdings) Hong Kong Ltd and Hongkong China Ltd for HK$696.99 million.
Lippo said it had agreed to sell the entire share capital of Chung Po Investment and Development Co Ltd for HK$282.58 million to Hongkong China.

Chung Po holds a stake in Zhuhai Chung Po House Property Development Co Ltd, a sino co-operative foreign joint venture established to develop Lippo CTS Plaza at Gongbei Port in Zhuhai, in China's southern province of Guangdong.

Lippo also agreed to sell Fulford Investment Ltd to Hongkong China for HK$44.23 million. Fulford holds an interest in Guangzhou Jikoon Property Development Co Ltd, a joint venture developing Guangzhou's Huang Sha Station Metro Line 1.
Huang Sha Station Site is proposed to be developed into a high-rise residential/commercial building, the statement said.

Lippo's 60 percent owned unit has also agreed to sell to China Travel Service (Holdings) Hong Kong Ltd the entire share capital of Jadeland Properties Ltd and 80 percent of Dorway Properties Ltd for an aggregate HK$370.18 million.

Jadeland and China Travel Service hold a respective 37.5 and 62.5 percent stake in China Travel Lippo Development (Hong Kong) Ltd, which indirectly participates in a China property development project through Oriental Light International Ltd.
China Travel Service is the controlling shareholder of China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd.

Dorway holds a stake in Guangzhou Jie-Chung Po Real Estate Development Ltd, a joint venture engaged in developing a site at Metro Line 1 in Guangzhou into a high rise hotel, office and commercial building.
Hongkong China, a 72.6 percent owned unit of Lippo, said the deal would provide it attractive opportunities to increase its land bank in China.

Lippo said the deal would streamline and rationalise the corporate structures and businesses of both the Lippo group and Hongkong China group and would concentrate property related business in the Hongkong China group.
Lippo said it would continue to concentrate on its other businesses such as financial services, insurance and securities trading. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
